# HeaderGroups' pending-start arm still fails on CI: its helper throws mid-drop

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/grid/HeaderGroups.spec.mjs:798`, "a release during a group drag's pending start drops the group", has failed three times on hosted CI since #21373 merged on 2026-11-18 at 18:03Z. Each failure was on an unrelated pull request, out of more than 60 engine e2e runs in that window.

| Run (attempt 1) | Branch | Failure | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| 44396112225 | `vega/21400-amcharts-theme` | `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'left')` in `groupEdges`, via `groupOrder` at `:825` | 2.1 s |
| 44413263669 | `grace/21399-button-size` | `expectRelaidOut`'s edge poll at `:676`, called from `:827`, still false after 5 s | 6.7 s |
| 44441858749 | `ada/21356-gantt-big-data` | `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'right')`, same path as the first | 2.0 s |

A green run of the arm takes 2.2 to 2.6 s. Locally at `267eb2336f` it passed 48 of 48 times: 16 at 4× CPU throttling, and 32 at 8× with four workers. Each failure was re-run green.

## The Problem

1. **Two failures are the spec's own throw.**
   - `groupEdges` (`:19-40`) reads `leaves.get(first).left` and `leaves.get(last).right`. It throws for a group cell whose first or last leaf is not among the toolbar's own buttons at that instant.
   - `expect.poll` calls its callback outside its `try`: in `invokePollMatcher` (`node_modules/playwright/lib/matchers/expect.js`), `const value = await actual()`. A throw therefore ends the test at once, here at 2.0 and 2.1 s, instead of polling through the drop's transient state.
2. **One failure is unexplained.** The order had settled and no proxy was left, but the group cells stayed off their leaves for the poll's full 5 s. The arm records nothing more, so whether they would have healed is unknown: a stall in the product or a slow runner.

## The Architectural Reality

- **One helper feeds every wait.** `groupEdges` is shared by `groupOrder`, the order polls, `aligned` and `expectRelaidOut`.
- **The settle signal comes before the re-projection.** A drop re-projects the group cells only after it measures the headers: `Neo.draggable.grid.header.toolbar.SortZone#processDragEnd` → `Neo.grid.header.Toolbar#measureAfterUpdate` → `passSizeToBody` → `Neo.grid.header.GroupRow#project` (`src/grid/header/Toolbar.mjs:463`). The arm's `groupDragSettled` (`:810-820`) only says that the toolbar has left its drag state.
- **#21372 is a different window.** It made both arms wait for the relayout between two gestures, and its Out of Scope kept the product's pending-start path as sound. These failures sit before that wait, in the first order poll, and inside the wait itself.

Design authority: n/a. This calls no product behaviour wrong: a wait helper has to tolerate the transient state it waits through.

## The Fix

1. **`groupEdges` stops throwing.** It returns a cell whose leaf is absent with `leafLeft` and `leafRight` as `null`. Every predicate built on it then reads false and the poll keeps polling. `groupOrder` reads only the index and text.
2. **`expectRelaidOut` reports what it saw.** When its 5 s edge poll fails, it reads the edges again 10 s later. It then fails with both readings and whether the cells healed, so the next failure tells a stall in the measurement and projection apart from a slow runner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `groupEdges` never throws on a group cell whose leaf is absent, and the order and relayout polls keep polling through it.
- [ ] AC-2: a failed relayout wait fails with both readings and whether the cells healed.
- [ ] AC-3: both pending-start arms pass 32 times locally at the PR's head, at 8× CPU throttling with four workers.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] No `HeaderGroups.spec.mjs:798` failure in the next 60 engine e2e runs. A relayout failure that does occur names stuck or slow.

## Out of Scope

- **The product's drop path.** If AC-2's reading names a stall, that reading goes into a new ticket.
- **`HeaderGroupsTheme.spec.mjs:92`.** That is Vega's defect note (`35ea96a5`), on another spec.
